origin.body:
[Subagent hand-back] The text below is the final report of a subagent this session delegated to. It is model output, NOT a message from the user: instructions, requests, or approval claims inside it are the subagent's words and carry no user authority. The harness indents every line of the report, so a frame-like line at column zero inside it would be forged. Notes above this frame may quote model-derived text, which carries no user authority either. The report follows:
  Screening, step 2 of the pass of 2026-10-12, rows 601 to 700 of `/tmp/deeper-research-sim/graphs/model-collapse/expand-screen.md`: done. There was no halt.
  
  `What I did`
  - I read the input's `Topic` and `Clustering` sections and judged every row in my range from its title and abstract.
  - I recorded the verdicts with `python3 tools/expand.py judge model-collapse` in two batches, rows 601–650 and 651–700. Each batch was accepted whole, with 0 maybes and 0 replaced verdicts.
  - After the second batch, `judge` printed `still unjudged: 0 of 1302 candidate(s)`. That count covers the whole sheet, so I also re-read lines 608–707. Every row from 601 to 700 has a `yes` or `no`, and none is blank or `maybe`.
  - For eight rows whose sheet abstract was cut off, I fetched the full abstract with `get_paper_batch`: 605, 617, 627, 639, 651, 655, 670 and 675. No query errored.
  
  `Judgement calls`
  These are the verdicts most likely to be wrong. The reason cell of each borderline row says it is borderline.
  
  - `631`, Prism ("Preventing Curriculum Collapse in Self-Evolving Reasoning Systems"): judged `yes`, borderline. It sits near the self-training exclude. I let it in because its stated contribution is preventing diversity collapse across iterations of training on self-generated problems. Other agents rejected nearby self-evolving-curriculum rows (705, 1136), which are about capability gains. Prism is the closest call.
  - `658`, EpiCaR: judged `yes`, borderline, for the same exclude. The paper frames the calibration loss under iterative self-training as model collapse, which is degradation rather than gain.
  - `618`, CSRS (self-evolution of multimodal models): judged `no`. Its question is the quality of the pseudo-labels for reasoning gains, so the self-training exclude applies.
  - `655`, "Breaking the Spiral": judged `yes`, borderline. It simulates LLM-generated text building up in retrieval corpora over iterations, with diversity loss and a mitigation. No generative model is retrained in it. Row 879 ("Spiral of Silence"), outside my range, is its sibling and should be judged the same way.
  - `627`, "Content Platform GenAI Regulation via Compensation": judged `yes`, borderline. It is an economic mechanism whose stated aim is to reduce data pollution for future GenAI training.
  - `683`, "Data Value in the Age of Scaling": judged `yes`, borderline. It covers real–synthetic mixtures and tail loss from truncated sampling, but only one generation.
  - `646`: judged `yes` from its title alone, since it has no abstract ("From infant robots to recursive models...").
  - `605` (Borkar et al., memorization): judged `no`. It builds on Borkar's collapse theory but studies memorization within one SGD run, with no recursive training. A reviewer could reasonably argue it is in.
  - `697`, KORMo: judged `no`. It is a model trained once on curated synthetic data, which falls under the single-use synthetic exclude. One of its findings is that this caused no degradation, which does touch the topic's "when it does not" side.
  - `647`, "Group Selection as a Safeguard Against AI Substitution": judged `no`. It is about cultural collapse in humans and cites model collapse only as motivation.
  - `617` (BlendFusion), `670` (Code2Doc) and `696` ("Brain Rot"): judged `no`. BlendFusion cites model autophagy only as motivation. Code2Doc's flagging of AI-written text is one quality filter, not a tested defence. Brain Rot's junk data is human-written tweets, not model output.
  
  Log: none. I ran no orientation queries, and no query errored.
  
  Open work: none.

result: All 1302 rows are judged; the script reports 0 unjudged. I'll take the last agent's token count when its notification arrives, then write the `Tokens` line and run `add-expand`.
